title: The shared setup document
description:
The one document every peer edits and every machine carries a copy of. The agent stores its bytes and reads only the `controller` block; everything else is for the clients. Unknown keys are allowed ANYWHERE and MUST be preserved when a client edits the document: a client that round-trips through a typed model and drops a key it did not know silently deletes another peer's newer setting, and the canonical hash then makes that deletion look like a legitimate edit. Edit the parsed JSON, not the model.

This file is not a reply. It is validated by contract/validate.mjs so that the client editors and the example configs agree about a shape none of them owns alone.

version.description: Stays 1. A bump would make every 1.2 client refuse a document for keys it can safely ignore, and every addition below is additive.

sites.description: Where the LANs are. Optional: a setup with one network does not need them.

appUpdates.description: Where every client looks for its own updates. Launch value: see contract §9.9.

local.description: DEPRECATED. Local control is a private per-device binding now; see bindings.schema.json. Read for compatibility and never written by a 1.3 editor. It is not stripped automatically: removing it would change the bytes, and therefore the hash, on whichever device happened to open the document first. Launch value: see contract §9.9.

ssh.description: DEPRECATED at the top level for the same reason as `local`.

controllerBlock.description: Who this setup is and where this copy sits in its history. `id` is the SETUP id, shared by every peer and stable for the life of the setup; it identified a device before the peer amendment and no longer does.

name.description: Display only. The name of the setup, not of a device.

revision.description: Monotonic within one id: 1 + the highest revision of every parent. It orders documents from one writer and CANNOT detect divergence, which is what `lineage` is for. The agent never decides acceptance from it.

updatedAt.description: Display only. Never compared: peers have no shared clock.

source.description: The kind of client that wrote this revision. Not a device identity and not a privilege.

device.description: Free text name of the device that wrote it, so a divergence screen can say who made each side.

site.description: One network. Two sites may have IDENTICAL private subnets, because home routers ship the same defaults, so a prefix match is a HINT and never proof of location: a client that matches more than one site must treat its location as unconfirmed rather than picking the first. What authenticates a machine is its pinned ssh host key, never its address.

lanPrefixes.description: IPv4 prefixes, dotted (`192.168.1.`: one to three octets, trailing dot recommended) or CIDR (`192.168.16.0/20`, length 8–32, no host bits). See contract §10.1. Anything else never matches and is reported as a warning.

broadcast.description: Dotted IPv4 broadcast addresses for machines at this site that name none of their own. Other entries are ignored.

site.description: Which site this machine is on. Must name an entry in sites[] when sites[] is non-empty (contract §9.7, unknown-site). A machine that names no site in sites[] is placed by wake.lanPrefix alone, or not at all: then direct wake is impossible and helpers still work (contract §10.1).

alwaysOn.description: A hint, used only for text. A wake path whose only helpers are not alwaysOn is worth warning about, because the user's whole reason for this design was not leaving a tower running.

ssh.description: DEPRECATED in the shared document: an identityFile is an absolute path on one device and means nothing on the others. Read for compatibility, never written by a 1.3 editor, never stripped automatically. Its host, user and port are held to the same guards as an endpoint's. Launch value: see contract §9.9.

id.description: Unique among the machine's endpoints. Optional, but an endpoint without an id cannot be remembered as a route, is never a duplicate, and merges together with the machine's other id-less endpoints as one entry (contract §9.7, §9.8).

kind.description: lan is dialled first when the controller is on the machine's site; remote otherwise.

system.description: Which system answers here on a dual-boot machine. A ROUTING HINT only: a status reporting a different system.id is still accepted, and the route is then re-remembered.

broadcast.description: Dotted IPv4 broadcast addresses. When there are none: the site's `broadcast`, then the directed broadcast of the controller's address on that network, then 255.255.255.255 (contract §10.2). Other entries are ignored.

ports.description: UDP ports. Entries outside 1–65535 are ignored; none means [9, 7].

probe.description: Not used by contract 3 clients: readiness is an authenticated status poll, never a TCP probe. Kept for 1.2 documents.

lanPrefix.description: DEPRECATED alias, used only when the machine names no site in sites[]. Same grammar as sites[].lanPrefixes.

helper.description: Compatibility alias for helpers[0]. An editor that writes `helpers` MUST also write this, so a 1.2 client keeps the one helper it understands. A 1.2 client does not do failover and must not be described as if it did.

helpers.description: Ordered failover. Walked in order; after a helper reports `ran` the client waits for the target and moves on only if it does not answer. Helpers are never woken automatically: a cascade would quietly turn the always-off tower into an always-on one, which is the thing this design exists to avoid.

helper.description: A machine that can wake this one, and the configured agent action on it that does the waking. No new wire verb: the client runs `run <action>` on the helper.

platform.description: The operating system this system runs. Launch value: see contract §9.9.

shell.description: The remote login shell, so a client quotes for the right one. Stock Windows OpenSSH defaults to cmd; a machine configured with PowerShell as its ssh shell needs powershell. A client that cannot quote for the configured shell says so rather than guessing. Launch value: see contract §9.9.

restricted.description: This system's key is bound to the restricted forced-command dispatcher. The dispatcher is not a shell: it parses a limited quoted argv grammar and never expands anything, so a client MUST serialise POSIX argv for it whatever `shell` says. Default false. Launch value: see contract §9.9.

agent.description: The argv that runs the agent. Empty, like absent, means not driven. Launch value: contract §9.9.
